citations.anchor: With this interim final rule, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations’ (EAR) controls on advanced computing integrated circuits (ICs) and adds a new control on artificial intelligence (AI) model weights for certain advanced closed-weight dual-use AI models.

statement: BIS's rule 2026-14132 states that, although § 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) of the EAR specifies a worldwide license requirement for certain advanced computing items (ECCNs 3A090.a, 4A090.a and related '.z' paragraph items), consistent with guidance issued on 13 May 2025 (cited by a bis.gov press-release address that includes the words 'rescission-biden-era') and on 31 May 2026, BIS is only enforcing this license requirement to destinations in Country Groups D:1, D:4 or D:5 (excluding those also in Country Groups A:5 or A:6) and to entities headquartered in, or with an ultimate parent headquartered in, Country Group D:5 or Macau.

citations.locator: p.3, 'Enforcement of License Requirements for Advanced Computing Items'
citations.anchor: Although § 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) of the EAR specifies a worldwide license requirement for certain advanced computing items (ECCNs 3A090.a, 4A090.a, and related ‘‘.z’’ paragraph items), consistent with guidance issued on May 13, 2025 (bis.gov/press-release/ department-commerce-announcesrescission-biden-era-artificialintelligence-diffusion-rule-strengthens) and May 31, 2026 (https://www.bis.gov/ media/documents/bis-guidance-may-312026.pdf), BIS is only enforcing this license requirement to destinations in Country Groups D:1, D:4, or D:5 (excluding those also specified in Country Groups A:5 or A:6), and to entities headquartered in or with an ultimate parent headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau, wherever located.
